issues.description: Same nil-guard boilerplate copy-pasted into ~20 accessors instead of one helper
issues.detail: Every getter opens with `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(x, ...)`. The fix should push nil-tolerance into one helper (or into seq.NewFixedSlice / the receiver types) so each getter is one line and future accessors cannot drift. You removed the panics by adding a special case everywhere instead of removing the special case.

issues.description: Two parallel nil-zero idioms coexist in one package (`f == nil` vs `IsZero()`)
issues.detail: *File methods guard with `f == nil` while Type/Member/Oneof/ReservedName/Element guard with `!x.IsZero()`. Pick one canonical predicate (e.g. always IsZero, with *File.IsZero defined as `f == nil`) so the rule is uniform across the IR and substitution is consistent for future accessors.

issues.description: Zero-value ADT contract is implicit; only enforced by a reflective test
issues.detail: The PR establishes a real contract that every accessor on a zero/nil receiver returns the zero of its result type, with documented exceptions. State this promise in package-level docs (e.g. on IsZero or doc.go) so subtypes and new methods know the precondition, instead of relying on reflection to discover violations after the fact.

issues.description: Reflection-driven zero test is too clever and silently skips methods with parameters
issues.detail: testZeroAny walks NumMethod, special-cases names like IsZero/ValueNodeIndex/Context, filters to NumIn==1, and treats any return with Len()==0 as success. Accessors taking arguments are never exercised, and new return types with a Len method silently pass. A boring explicit per-type table of (name, func(T) any) would be longer but obvious and durable.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex returns -1 sentinel, inconsistent with rest of the zero-value API
issues.detail: Every other zero accessor returns the zero of its return type; ValueNodeIndex returns -1, so callers must know two sentinels. Either return (int, bool) / add a HasValueNode predicate, or surface the precondition on the Element type itself rather than burying it in a doc-comment and reflect special-case.

issues.description: Test fixes and behavioral nil-guards should be split into separate commits
issues.detail: The PR mixes adding the zero test with ~20 behavioral nil-guard fixes. Land the test first (red), then each panic fix as its own diff with a one-line justification, so future bisects on regressions in File.Imports() and similar accessors point at a meaningful commit instead of "add zero test."

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the intent is sound — making the zero value a first-class member of each IR type's ADT and enforcing it with a sweep test is good discipline. The execution has three recurring complaints: the same nil-guard boilerplate is copy-pasted into ~20 accessors instead of pushed into a helper or the data structure; two different zero idioms (`f == nil` vs `IsZero()`) coexist in one package; and the contract itself lives only in a reflective test rather than in package docs. The test is valuable but too clever — reflection plus name-based special cases will fail confusingly when future accessors drift. Lands after consolidation; not a blocker but needs-work.
